newsitem.title: UK: British pop "bad boy" Gallagher in drugs probe.
newsitem.headline: British pop "bad boy" Gallagher in drugs probe.

text.p: Oasis lead singer Liam Gallagher, known as the bad boy of British pop, was arrested in London on Saturday on suspicion of possessing cocaine.
Police said Gallagher was stopped early in the morning in London's Oxford Street shopping district and taken to a nearby police station.
He was not formally charged but a substance was taken away for analysis and 24-year-old Gallagher was ordered to report back to police on December 30.

His arrest was the latest in a series of headline-grabbing antics surrounding Oasis, which has rocketed to success in the past three years to become the most successful British pop band since The Beatles in the 1960s.
Gallagher and his song-writing brother Noel have made bad behaviour and foul language their hallmark since the Manchester-based band burst onto the scene in 1993.
Liam once boasted: "We are bigger than Jesus. We will be as big as the Beatles, if not bigger."
Journalists and photographers outside the brothers' London home on Saturday were given a typical reaction -- two fingers stuck up through a half-open door. The band has made no other comment.
In September, Liam left the band half-way through a tour of the United States and the tour was cancelled, fuelling rumours that Oasis was splitting up.
In an outburst at the time, Noel Gallagher told reporters: "I don't give a f*** about America as long as they buy the f***ing records."
The rumours of a split were denied although their record company said Oasis would not be touring for "the forseeable future".
Liam Gallagher was arrested only hours after picking up an award from British style magazine Q for Best Act in the World and delivering a feisty insult to the VIP audience.
Earlier this week, a shocked pop fan claimed Liam bit her nose during a concert in London.
Oasis's first two albums "Definitely Maybe" and "Morning Glory" sold 20 million copies and led a British pop revival.
A summer concert in Britain drew a record crowd of 250,000 -- the biggest British paying audience for a single act in the history of rock and roll.
